hypothesis_h0: The gain is absent, or it is an artefact of the asymmetric selection rule: applying the same cost rule to the event family (symmetric arm) reverses the sign, and a fine-grid budget-matched EWMA scanner is within 0.2 pp of the event controller.
hypothesis_h1: In an independently generated frozen-bank world (8 regimes, persistence 320, delay 2, 4,096 batches), the fixed CUSUM event controller (theta 0.5, gamma 0.8) beats the cost-selected EWMA scanner by at least 0.25 percentage points of whole-stream accuracy.
notes: Verdict is on the primary contrast only. The interpretation key is the pair of secondary contrasts (event_fixed - adaptive_budget_fine) and (event_cost_selected_sym - adaptive_accuracy_first): if the first is within +/-0.2 pp and the second is negative, the original gain is attributed to the selection rule, not to the detector. Work per input, final-quarter accuracy and scan counts are recorded as extras.
source_claim: At persistence 320, delay 2, 4,096 batches, all four widths show positive whole-stream accuracy gains against the cost-selected adaptive controller: +0.358 to +0.400 pp (lower CI bounds +0.22 to +0.27) with +0.46% to +5.47% extra work. 'The long-run accuracy gain is real, with a measurable price.'
title: Expert switching: event controller long-run accuracy gain vs cost-selected adaptive scanner
